sections.overview: Meleager’s Blue is a locally distributed blue butterfly of southeastern Europe and western Asia.
sections.identification: Both sexes have scalloped hindwing edges, especially pronounced in females. Males are blue above; females are usually brown, sometimes with blue at the wing bases.
sections.habitat: It inhabits warm, dry, often flowery grasslands, scrub edges and woodland clearings, from low hills to about eighteen hundred metres in some regional accounts.
sections.diet: Adults take nectar from flowers. Caterpillars feed on legumes, including crown vetch and milk-vetches such as Astragalus.
sections.behavior: It usually has one generation per year, with adults flying in summer; populations can be local and small.
sections.reproduction: It overwinters as an egg or young larva, depending on the region. Caterpillars may be attended by ants.
sections.ecology: Its scalloped hindwing margin is a useful distinction from many other blue butterflies. A Central European population study found high densities near patches of the larval host plant Securigera varia.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted describe it as local in parts of its range but do not provide a current global IUCN category.
